validity.recommendation: SUPERSEDED IN PART -- do NOT treat this row as a deletion candidate. The redundancy leg's cluster-E record on this row is the ruling: keep P1846, downgrade to 'single-sourced, faithfully transcribed'. The residual concerns from this record that DO still stand: (a) the row is single-sourced on one OPEC operator return, so a second independent source is still wanted; (b) do not fill further specs off that single source; (c) re-point the dead opec.org citations to the Wayback ASB URLs.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE (primary concern). The row's only support is generic and does not name the line. The gem.wiki page (read for leads only, not cited) carries a single reference: 'Annual Statistics Bulletin, OPEC, 2012, p.75'. I ran that PDF through url_verifier for the token 'Kabesa' -> FAIL (200 but token absent): the OPEC aggregate bulletin does not mention this pipeline. The gem.wiki record is otherwise skeletal: no StartLocation/EndLocation (worklist shows only StartCountryOrArea=Iraq, EndCountryOrArea=Iraq), no start year, no narrative. Independent searching (EN + AR, incl. Iraqi press, and the Al-Jibawi 2025 'Shedding Light on Recent Oil & Gas Pipeline Projects in Iraq' review) surfaced ZERO sources naming a 'Strategic-Kabesa Cement' gas pipeline, and none for its 2023-09-09 sibling cluster (P1847 Strategic-Hilla, P1848 Strategic-Najaf) either. The only corroborated fact is that the destination plant is real: Kubaisa (Al-Kubaisa) Cement Plant in the Hit district of western Al-Anbar, ~1.7-2 Mt/y, ISIS-damaged then rehabilitated (Shafaq EN + AR). But no source documents a gas line serving it, and the Arabic reporting explicitly notes no such gas line is described. Geography compounds the doubt: Iraq's operating gas grid runs from the south/Basra up to Baghdad and from the center to meet the northern (Kirkuk) network, feeding power stations at Nasiriyah, Hartha, Khor al-Zubair and Najaf (rawabetcenter) -- it does NOT reach western Anbar. Anbar's own gas (Akkas field) is essentially undeveloped, so there is no plausible gas source for a 39 km spur to Kubaisa. SECONDARY concern_type=classification: the 'Strategic-<destination>' naming pattern matches branches off the crude-oil Iraq Strategic Pipeline, not a gas system -- cf. GulfPub 'Musaiab Power Station Line | Strategic Pipeline, Karbala -> Musaiab Power Station' (16in, OPC), a fuel/crude feeder. The gem.wiki 'Iraq Strategic Pipeline' page is unambiguously the 42in crude oil line (Basra-Haditha). If this row corresponds to anything real, it is more likely a fuel-oil/crude feeder to the cement plant mislabeled as gas than a genuine gas transmission trunk. SPEC concern: the stated 0.67 bcm/y is implausibly large for a single ~2 Mt/y cement plant (typical kiln gas demand ~0.1-0.15 bcm/y), and length (39 km), diameter (10 in) and capacity are all unsourced (the sole OPEC cite lacks the line). Owner 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' is likewise unsupported by any independent source naming this asset. Net: no independent evidence this pipeline physically exists as described; treat as phantom/misclassified pending review. || SUPERSEDED 2026-07-28 on the deletion question. This record's 'strong candidate for deletion' rested on url_verifier FAILing to find the token 'Kabesa' in the OPEC ASB PDF, which I read as the bulletin not naming the pipeline. That was a VERIFIER LIMIT, not an absence: the redundancy leg read the PDF directly and found the row verbatim -- ASB Table 4.10/9.9 is a PER-PIPELINE table whose first column is 'Connection from/to', and this row's entry is 'Strategy/Kabesa Cement | OPC | 24 | 10 in | 671,000', with the ASB diameter 10 in matching GEM's 10.00. So the row is a faithful 1:1 transcription of a named source row, not a GEM construction. The general lesson, which is why this is escalated as a class and not just fixed here: a url_verifier token FAIL on a large PDF is not evidence that the source lacks the value -- see notes/escalation-2026-07-28-asb-iraq-provenance.md and the six known false-negative families. My 'ZERO sources name this line' finding stands only for sources OTHER than the ASB itself.

routes.start_name: Unresolved (no documented gas source; 'Strategic' origin undefined -- western Anbar is not reached by Iraq's operating gas grid)
routes.end_name: Kubaisa (Al-Kubaisa) Cement Plant, near Kubaisa town, Hit district, Al-Anbar, Iraq
routes.corridor_desc: Only the nominal destination can be located: the Kubaisa/Al-Kubaisa Cement Plant sits beside Kubaisa (Kabisa) town in the Hit district of western Al-Anbar (town coord 33.593N, 42.616E per Wikipedia; the plant is immediately adjacent, not separately geocoded here). No start point or corridor can be defended: no independent source gives endpoints for this line, the record itself lists only 'Iraq -> Iraq', and there is no operating gas source in western Anbar (the Akkas field is undeveloped; the national gas grid terminates far to the east/south). This is a single-point bound around the cement plant, NOT a defensible corridor. Do not propose a route to the routes repo until the line's existence and true endpoints are established.
routes.researcher_notes: End coordinate is the Kubaisa (Kabisa) town centroid from Wikipedia (33 35 34N / 42 36 56E = 33.59278, 42.61556), Hit district, Al-Anbar -- verified via url_verifier (tokens 'Anbar','Hit' present). The cement plant lies at that town; I did not fabricate a plant-specific coordinate. Start point deliberately left null: no source establishes it and no gas source exists nearby. No fabricated coordinates.

summary: P1846 Strategic-Kabesa Cement Gas Pipeline: CONCERN (existence; secondary classification+spec) -- sole cite is generic OPEC ASB 2012 that doesn't name it, zero independent traces, no gas grid reaches western Anbar, 'Strategic-' pattern matches crude-oil branches; likely phantom or fuel-oil line mislabeled as gas.
